FAQ

While our company does not currently make gluten-free label claims, none of the ingredients in our products are derived from grains or flours that have been linked to malabsorption syndrome associated with gluten sensitivity.

Our beverages are shelf stable which means they don't need to be refrigerated prior to opening. However, we do recommend refrigeration after opening to maintain freshness.

No, Dr Pepper is not a PepsiCo product. Dr Pepper is owned and produced by Keurig Dr Pepper and has its own formulation and brand history. However, distribution can vary by region. In some markets, PepsiCo-affiliated bottlers distribute Dr Pepper products, while in other areas, distribution is handled by Coca-Cola–affiliated bottlers. 

When people ask if Dr Pepper is a Pepsi product, they usually mean PepsiCo, not Pepsi the legacy cola brand. Pepsi is a single cola brand, while PepsiCo is the parent company that owns many different brands. 

No matter who distributes it locally, Dr Pepper remains a distinct brand with its own ownership, recipe and product standards. If you’re looking for details about the Pepsi beverage lineup, you can explore our Products.  

Pepsi is owned by PepsiCo, Inc., a global food and beverage company with a long history of bringing iconic, beloved brands to people around the world. PepsiCo was formed in 1965 through the merger of the Pepsi-Cola Company and Frito-Lay, creating a company that combines beverages and foods under one organization. 

Today, PepsiCo owns and manages the Pepsi brand along with many other brands you may recognize. As a publicly traded company, PepsiCo is owned by shareholders and operates independently, focusing on innovation, quality and responsible business practices. You can explore more about PepsiCo brands and products by visiting our site here.  

Yes, Mountain Dew is a PepsiCo product. Mountain Dew has been part of the PepsiCo family for decades and is one of the company’s most recognizable beverage brands. Known for its bold citrus flavor, Mountain Dew has grown to include a variety of flavors and limited-time offerings enjoyed by fans worldwide. 

As with all PepsiCo beverages, Mountain Dew is produced and distributed with a focus on quality, safety and great taste. PepsiCo continues to evolve the Mountain Dew brand through innovation while maintaining the flavor that people know and love.

Yes, Pepsi Zero Sugar contains caffeine. As with all our beverages, the presence of caffeine is clearly labeled in the ingredient statement and the amount of caffeine is shown on the product label.  

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

Diet Pepsi is safe to enjoy as part of a balanced lifestyle. It contains no sugar or calories, making it a popular choice for people looking to reduce sugar intake while still enjoying great taste.  

We encourage people to review the ingredient list and nutrition information found on the product label so they can make choices that are right for them.  

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

A 12-ounce can of Pepsi contains 38 milligrams of caffeine in the United States. The presence of any added caffeine in our beverages is clearly listed in the ingredient statement and the caffeine content is shown on the product label. 

Pepsi Max is a bold, great-tasting cola with no sugar or calories. It is made for people who want the great taste of Pepsi, all without sugar. Pepsi Max delivers the signature cola taste you expect, paired with a crisp, refreshing finish that sets it apart within the Pepsi family. 

Pepsi Max is available in select markets, such as the UK and Australia. It is sweetened with aspartame* and other low-calorie sweeteners.  

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

A 12-ounce can of Pepsi contains 41 grams of sugar. 

As consumer preference continues to evolve, so has our portfolio to provide people with greater optionality. Pepsi offers a wide range of beverage options, including no-sugar and zero-calorie choices like Pepsi Zero Sugar and Diet Pepsi, and a lower sugar option with functional ingredients like Pepsi Prebiotic Cola. Our full beverage lineup can be found here. 

No, Diet Pepsi does not contain sugar. Diet Pepsi is sweetened with a sugar substitute, making it a zero-sugar, zero-calorie option for consumers who want the refreshing, great taste of Pepsi without added sugar. 

Everyone’s tastes and nutritional goals are different, which is why Pepsi offers a wide range of beverage options within its portfolio, including regular Pepsi, Diet Pepsi and Pepsi Zero Sugar. We encourage consumers to review nutrition information on labels and choose the option that best fits their taste and lifestyle.  

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

Yes, Pepsi Zero Sugar is safe to drink. The ingredients used in Pepsi Zero Sugar have been thoroughly studied and reviewed by food safety experts.  

Pepsi Zero Sugar contains no sugar or calories while delivering the full bold Pepsi taste you expect, making it a popular choice for people looking to reduce sugar intake. Ingredient and nutrition information are always clearly listed on the product label so consumers can choose the beverage option that best fits their lifestyle and dietary goals. 

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

Yes, Diet Pepsi contains caffeine. As with all our beverages in the United States, if caffeine is presentrs, it is listed clearly in the ingredients and the caffeine content is shown on the product label. People who enjoy the taste of Diet Pepsi but prefer to avoid caffeine can opt for a separate product, Diet Pepsi Caffeine Free.  

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

A 12-ounce can of Diet Pepsi contains 35 milligrams of caffeine. As with all our beverages, caffeine is clearly listed in the ingredient statement and the amount is shown on the product label so consumers can make informed choices. 

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

Yes, Diet Pepsi contains aspartame*. Aspartame is a low-calorie sweetener that has been used in foods and beverages for decades. It allows Diet Pepsi to deliver the familiar sweet taste of Pepsi without adding sugar or calories. 

Aspartame is clearly listed on Diet Pepsi packaging. We encourage consumers to review product labels to make informed choices that fit their lifestyle.  

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

A 12-ounce can of Pepsi contains 41 grams of sugar. Nutrition information, including the exact amount of sugar, is clearly displayed on the product label so you can make informed decisions about what you drink.  

We know that consumers have different preferences and nutritional goals, which is why Pepsi offers a variety of beverage options. Consumers looking for reduced- or no-sugar options with the same great taste can choose Diet Pepsi or Pepsi Zero Sugar. Explore our Products for more information on our full beverage lineup.  

Crystal Pepsi was first introduced in 1992 as a clear cola with the same great taste of Pepsi. It was part of a wave of innovation at the time, offering a new look while keeping a familiar flavor. While Crystal Pepsi quickly became a pop culture favorite, it was originally available for a limited time and was discontinued in 1994.  

Over the years, Crystal Pepsi has made several special appearances through limited-time returns, often driven by fan enthusiasm and nostalgia. These re-releases gave longtime fans and new consumers a chance to experience the iconic clear cola.  

Crystal Pepsi is not part of the permanent Pepsi lineup, but it remains a memorable part of our brand’s history. Pepsi continues to explore new flavors and experiences while celebrating the products that have made a lasting impression along the way. Explore our Products for more information on our full beverage lineup. 

Pepsi has a bold, refreshing cola flavor that blends sweetness with citrus notes and a crisp finish. Its taste comes from a carefully balanced combination of ingredients that work together to create the signature flavor people recognize and enjoy around the world.  

The flavor of Pepsi has remained true to its roots throughout the decades while continuing to appeal to changing tastes. That classic cola profile has a more upfront sweetness and a lighter finish, creating a soda  that can be enjoyed on its own or with food 

Pepsi also offers a variety of cola Products, including zero-sugar, flavored and prebiotic versions. Each builds upon the classic taste of Pepsi while offering different flavor twists and profiles, allowing consumers to choose the taste experience that suits their taste and preferences. 

Diet Pepsi and Pepsi Zero Sugar are both sugar-free and calorie-free colas offering cola and soda-lovers more ways to enjoy the great taste of Pepsi. 

Diet Pepsi has been a classic choice for decades and is known for its light, crisp classic flavor. Pepsi Zero Sugar has a slightly richer cola taste. 

Both are crafted with a blend of low-calorie sweeteners, including aspartame* and acesulfame potassium. 

Both are great options for those looking for sugar- and calorie-free cola or soda, and we encourage you to try both to find your preference.  

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

Yes, Pepsi Zero Sugar contains caffeine. Pepsi Zero Sugar is formulated to deliver bold Pepsi taste with no sugar or calories, and caffeine is part of that flavor experience. As with all our beverages, the presence of caffeine is clearly listed in the ingredient statement and the amount of caffeine is shown on the product label.  

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine 

A 12-ounce can of Pepsi contains 150 calories. Pepsi offers a variety of beverage options to suit different lifestyles, preferences and dietary options. That’s why Pepsi also offers soda choices like Pepsi Zero Sugar, Diet Pepsi, Pepsi Zero Sugar Wild Pepsi, Diet Pepsi Wild Cherry, Diet Pepsi Caffeine Free, Pepsi Zero Sugar Wild Cherry and Cream, Pepsi Prebiotic Cola and Pepsi Prebiotic Cola Cherry Vanilla – which contain lower or zero calories.  

Nutrition information, including calorie content, is always clearly listed on the product label so consumers can make informed decisions. 

Yes, Pepsi Zero Sugar contains aspartame* and other no-calorie sweeteners. Pepsi Zero Sugar is formulated to taste like original Pepsi, and the combination of sweeteners plays an important role in achieving that flavor profile. 

*Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine  

Pepsi was invented by Caleb Davis Bradham, an American pharmacist from New Bern, North Carolina. In the summer of 1893, Bradham began experimenting with soft drink recipes at the soda fountain in his drugstore. His most popular creation was a sweet, bubbly beverage originally intended as a refreshing drink to be enjoyed with food. At the time, it was known as “Brad’s Drink.” 

The beverage was officially renamed Pepsi-Cola in 1898. The name “Pepsi” was inspired in part by the term “dyspepsia,” reflecting Bradham’s belief that the drink could help with digestion. As the popularity of Pepsi continued to grow, Bradham incorporated the first Pepsi-Cola Company in 1902. 

What began as a local soda fountain favorite quickly grew into a globally-beloved brand. Today, Pepsi continues to build on the legacy of innovation that started more than a century ago with a lineup of Products billions of people love.

Crystal Pepsi is one of the most unique and memorable Pepsi products, known for being a clear, caffeine-free cola. It was originally introduced in the United States and Canada in 1992. While it looked different from traditional colas, Crystal Pepsi was created to deliver the familiar Pepsi taste without the caramel color of traditional cola. 

Marketed with the slogan “You’ve never seen a taste like this,” Crystal Pepsi captured attention and became a defining product of the early 1990s. Although its initial run  came to an end in 1994, the beverage earned a lasting place in pop culture. 

Over the years, strong fan enthusiasm has inspired several limited-time returns, giving people the chance to enjoy this nostalgic twist on a classic cola. While Crystal Pepsi is a permanent Pepsi Product offered today, it remains a standout example of Pepsi’s innovative spirit and creativity. 

Pepsi Prebiotic Cola combines the iconic Pepsi taste people love with functional  ingredients, including 3 grams of prebiotic fiber* in every 12-ounce can. This prebiotic soda is made with no artificial sweeteners and contains 5 grams of sugar per 12-ounce can.  

This refreshing cola is designed for consumers looking for functional ingredients without sacrificing taste. It delivers the unmistakable Pepsi flavor that elevates food and everyday moments, while offering an additional choice among Pepsi Products to meet evolving consumer interests. As always, ingredient and nutrition information are clearly listed on the label so consumers can choose what works best for them. 

* +10 g of soluble corn fiber daily has been shown to provide a prebiotic effect. This product provides 3 g of soluble corn fiber.    

Yes, Starry is a PepsiCo product. It is a crisp, clear and refreshing lemon-lime flavored soda introduced in 2023. It offers bold flavor without caffeine and is available in both Regular and Zero Sugar varieties. Like other PepsiCo beverages, Starry is produced and distributed with a focus on quality and great taste. 

Starry delivers a bright lemon-lime flavor and is part of PepsiCo’s broader portfolio of beverages enjoyed by consumers across the U.S. If you’re looking for information on our full range of PepsiCo products, from classic Pepsi to newer offerings like Starry, you can explore the beverage lineup here.  

When people ask if Starry is a Pepsi product, they usually mean PepsiCo, not Pepsi the cola brand. Pepsi is a single cola brand, while PepsiCo is the parent company that owns many different brands. 

No, Sunkist is produced and distributed by Keurig Dr Pepper and is not a PepsiCo product. Since beverage distribution varies by country or region, you may occasionally see Sunkist alongside PepsiCo products in some locations. This is due to local bottling or distribution agreements. 

When people ask if Sunkist is a Pepsi product, they usually mean PepsiCo, not Pepsi the cola brand. Pepsi is a single cola brand, while PepsiCo is the parent company that owns many different brands. 

If you’re looking for details about the Pepsi beverage lineup, you can explore our Products. 

No, 7UP is not a PepsiCo product in the United States. When people ask if 7UP is a Pepsi product, they usually mean PepsiCo, not Pepsi the cola brand. Pepsi is a single cola brand, while PepsiCo is the parent company that owns many different brands. Additionally, In the U.S., 7UP is owned and distributed by Keurig Dr Pepper. 

However, in international markets outside the U.S., 7UP is owned and distributed by PepsiCo and is part of the PepsiCo beverage portfolio in those regions. This means that while 7UP is not a PepsiCo product for U.S. consumers, it is closely connected to PepsiCo in other parts of the world. 

If you’re looking for details about the Pepsi beverage lineup in the United States, you can explore our Products.  

The brand Pepsi is part of PepsiCo, a global food and beverage company that offers much more than its iconic cola. PepsiCo’s portfolio includes a wide range of popular and trusted brands across snacks, beverages and convenient foods. This diverse lineup began taking shape in 1965 with the merger of Pepsi-Cola and Frito-Lay and has continued to grow over the years. 

Today, PepsiCo owns many well-known brands. Some of the most recognizable names include Pepsi, Lay’s, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Mountain Dew, Quaker, Propel and SodaStream. 

PepsiCo continues to expand and evolve its portfolio to offer choices that fit different tastes, occasions and lifestyles. Since availability can vary by region, not every brand is sold everywhere. You can explore more about PepsiCo’s brands and products by visiting our site here. 

In 1898, small-town pharmacist Caleb D. Bradham looked for a name that would better describe his formula -- which he was selling under the name "Brad's Drink." He bought the name "Pep Kola" from a local competitor and changed it to Pepsi-Cola.

The complete list of our products, their ingredients, and nutrition facts can be found here.

A 12-ounce can of  Pepsi   contains 41 grams of sugar. Nutrition information, including the exact amount of sugar, is clearly displayed on the product label so you can make informed decisions about what you drink.   We know that consumers have different preferences and nutritional goals, which is why Pepsi offers a variety of beverage options. Consumers looking for reduced- or no-sugar options with the same great taste can choose Diet Pepsi or Pepsi Zero Sugar. Explore our  Products  for more information on our full beverage lineup.   17. What happened to Crystal Pepsi? Crystal Pepsi was first introduced in 1992 as a clear cola with the same great taste of Pepsi. It was part of a wave of innovation at the time, offering a new look while keeping a familiar flavor. While Crystal Pepsi quickly became a pop culture favorite, it was originally available for a limited time and was discontinued in 1994.   Over the years, Crystal Pepsi has made several special appearances through limited-time returns, often driven by fan enthusiasm and nostalgia. These re-releases gave longtime fans and new consumers a chance to experience the iconic clear cola.   Crystal Pepsi is not part of the permanent Pepsi lineup, but it remains a memorable part of our brand’s history. Pepsi continues to explore new flavors and experiences while celebrating the products that have made a lasting impression along the way. Explore our  Products  for more information on our full beverage lineup.  18. What flavor is Pepsi? Pepsi   has a bold, refreshing cola flavor that blends sweetness with citrus notes and a crisp finish. Its taste comes from a carefully balanced combination of ingredients that work together to create the signature flavor people recognize and enjoy around the world.   The flavor of Pepsi has remained true to its roots throughout the decades while continuing to appeal to changing tastes. That classic cola profile has a more upfront sweetness and a lighter finish, creating a soda  that can be enjoyed on its own or with food  Pepsi also offers a variety of cola  Products , including zero-sugar, flavored and prebiotic versions. Each builds upon the classic taste of Pepsi while offering different flavor twists and profiles, allowing consumers to choose the taste experience that suits their taste and preferences.  19. What is the difference between Diet Pepsi and Pepsi Zero sugar? Diet Pepsi  and  Pepsi Zero Sugar  are both sugar-free and calorie-free colas offering cola and soda-lovers more ways to enjoy the great taste of Pepsi.  Diet Pepsi has been a classic choice for decades and is known for its light, crisp classic flavor. Pepsi Zero Sugar has a slightly richer cola taste.  Both are crafted with a blend of low-calorie sweeteners, including aspartame* and acesulfame potassium.  Both are great options for those looking for sugar- and calorie-free cola or soda, and we encourage you to try both to find your preference.   *Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine  20. Does Pepsi Zero sugar have caffeine? Yes,  Pepsi Zero Sugar  contains caffeine. Pepsi Zero Sugar is formulated to deliver bold Pepsi taste with no sugar or calories, and caffeine is part of that flavor experience. As with all our beverages, the presence of caffeine is clearly listed in the ingredient statement and the amount of caffeine is shown on the product label.   *Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine  21. How many calories are in a can of Pepsi? A 12-ounce can of  Pepsi  contains 150 calories. Pepsi offers a variety of beverage options to suit different lifestyles, preferences and dietary options. That’s why Pepsi also offers soda choices like Pepsi Zero Sugar, Diet Pepsi, Pepsi Zero Sugar Wild Pepsi, Diet Pepsi Wild Cherry, Diet Pepsi Caffeine Free, Pepsi Zero Sugar Wild Cherry and Cream, Pepsi Prebiotic Cola and Pepsi Prebiotic Cola Cherry Vanilla – which contain lower or zero calories.   Nutrition information, including calorie content, is always clearly listed on the product label so consumers can make informed decisions.  22. Does Pepsi Zero have aspartame? Yes,  Pepsi Zero Sugar  contains aspartame* and other no-calorie sweeteners. Pepsi Zero Sugar is formulated to taste like original Pepsi, and the combination of sweeteners plays an important role in achieving that flavor profile.  *Phenylketonurics: Contains Phenylalanine   23. Who invented Pepsi? Pepsi was invented by Caleb Davis Bradham, an American pharmacist from New Bern, North Carolina. In the summer of 1893, Bradham began experimenting with soft drink recipes at the soda fountain in his drugstore. His most popular creation was a sweet, bubbly beverage originally intended as a refreshing drink to be enjoyed with food. At the time, it was known as “Brad’s Drink.”  The beverage was officially renamed Pepsi-Cola in 1898. The name “Pepsi” was inspired in part by the term “dyspepsia,” reflecting Bradham’s belief that the drink could help with digestion. As the popularity of Pepsi continued to grow, Bradham incorporated the first Pepsi-Cola Company in 1902.  What began as a local soda fountain favorite quickly grew into a globally-beloved brand. Today, Pepsi continues to build on the legacy of innovation that started more than a century ago with a lineup of  Products   billions of people love. 24. What is Crystal Pepsi? Crystal Pepsi is one of the most unique and memorable Pepsi products, known for being a clear, caffeine-free cola. It was originally introduced in the United States and Canada in 1992. While it looked different from traditional colas, Crystal Pepsi was created to deliver the familiar Pepsi taste without the caramel color of traditional cola.  Marketed with the slogan “You’ve never seen a taste like this,” Crystal Pepsi captured attention and became a defining product of the early 1990s. Although its initial run  came to an end in 1994, the beverage earned a lasting place in pop culture.  Over the years, strong fan enthusiasm has inspired several limited-time returns, giving people the chance to enjoy this nostalgic twist on a classic cola. While Crystal Pepsi is a permanent Pepsi  Product  offered today, it remains a standout example of Pepsi’s innovative spirit and creativity.  25. What is in Pepsi Prebiotic soda? Pepsi Prebiotic Cola  combines the iconic Pepsi taste people love with functional  ingredients, including 3 grams of prebiotic fiber* in every 12-ounce can. This prebiotic soda is made with no artificial sweeteners and contains 5 grams of sugar per 12-ounce can.   This refreshing cola is designed for consumers looking for functional ingredients without sacrificing taste. It delivers the unmistakable Pepsi flavor that elevates food and everyday moments, while offering an additional choice among Pepsi  Products  to meet evolving consumer interests. As always, ingredient and nutrition information are clearly listed on the label so consumers can choose what works best for them.  * +10 g of soluble corn fiber daily has been shown to provide a prebiotic effect. This product provides 3 g of soluble corn fiber.     26. Is Starry a Pepsi product? Yes,  Starry   is a PepsiCo product. It is a crisp, clear and refreshing lemon-lime flavored soda introduced in 2023. It offers bold flavor without caffeine and is available in both Regular and Zero Sugar varieties. Like other PepsiCo beverages, Starry is produced and distributed with a focus on quality and great taste.  Starry delivers a bright lemon-lime flavor and is part of PepsiCo’s broader portfolio of beverages enjoyed by consumers across the U.S. If you’re looking for information on our full range of PepsiCo products, from classic Pepsi to newer offerings like Starry, you can explore the beverage lineup  here .   When people ask if Starry is a Pepsi product, they usually mean PepsiCo, not Pepsi the cola brand. Pepsi is a single cola brand, while PepsiCo is the parent company that owns many different brands.  27. Is Sunkist a Pepsi product? No, Sunkist is produced and distributed by Keurig Dr Pepper and is not a PepsiCo product. Since beverage distribution varies by country or region, you may occasionally see Sunkist alongside PepsiCo products in some locations. This is due to local bottling or distribution agreements.  When people ask if Sunkist is a Pepsi product, they usually mean PepsiCo, not Pepsi the cola brand. Pepsi is a single cola brand, while PepsiCo is the parent company that owns many different brands.  If you’re looking for details about the Pepsi beverage lineup, you can explore our  Products .  28. Is 7UP a Pepsi product? No, 7UP is not a PepsiCo product in the United States. When people ask if 7UP is a Pepsi product, they usually mean PepsiCo, not Pepsi the cola brand. Pepsi is a single cola brand, while PepsiCo is the parent company that owns many different brands. Additionally, In the U.S., 7UP is owned and distributed by Keurig Dr Pepper.  However, in international markets outside the U.S., 7UP is owned and distributed by PepsiCo and is part of the PepsiCo beverage portfolio in those regions. This means that while 7UP is not a PepsiCo product for U.S. consumers, it is closely connected to PepsiCo in other parts of the world.  If you’re looking for details about the Pepsi beverage lineup in the United States, you can explore our  Products .   29. What companies does Pepsi own? The brand Pepsi is part of PepsiCo, a global food and beverage company that offers much more than its iconic cola. PepsiCo’s portfolio includes a wide range of popular and trusted brands across snacks, beverages and convenient foods. This diverse lineup began taking shape in 1965 with the merger of Pepsi-Cola and Frito-Lay and has continued to grow over the years.  Today, PepsiCo owns many well-known brands. Some of the most recognizable names include Pepsi, Lay’s, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Mountain Dew, Quaker, Propel and SodaStream.  PepsiCo continues to expand and evolve its portfolio to offer choices that fit different tastes, occasions and lifestyles. Since availability can vary by region, not every brand is sold everywhere. You can explore more about PepsiCo’s brands and products by visiting our site  here .  30. When was Pepsi-Cola invented? How did it get its name? In 1898, small-town pharmacist Caleb D. Bradham looked for a name that would better describe his formula -- which he was selling under the name "Brad's Drink." He bought the name "Pep Kola" from a local competitor and changed it to Pepsi-Cola. 31. Where can I find information regarding nutrition and ingredients? The complete list of our products, their ingredients, and nutrition facts can be found  here .
